111100101.text: Wh—Why did we come here? Paimon's got a bad feeling about this...

111100102.text: Not that Paimon's scared or anything, just... concerned for your safety.

111100103.text: It's just that this is how lots of scary stories go — you're in an empty place in the middle of nowhere, there's barely any light, and then just when you least expect it, a stranger comes out of—

111100108.text: Paimon's intuition says that anyone we run into here is going to be far from normal!

111100109.text: If he gets us, he's gonna eat Paimon for sure!

subQuests.subQuestName: Catch up to the fleeing Meng

111100301.text: Director! Director! There's a ghost after me!

111100303.text: Ha, don't get too excited. These are clients, not ghosts.

111100304.text: Exactly! We said we're not ghosts. Why won't you calm down and let us explain?

111100305.text: Although... "clients" doesn't seem quite right either.

111100306.text: Aiya, forgive me, this is one of our new undertakers, Meng. It's his first time working a funeral, so of course, he's afraid of his own shadow.

111100307.text: Funeral... Funeral... Oh! The Wangsheng Funeral Parlor — Zhongli is a consultant there. They deal with this stuff a lot, right?

111100308.text: Oh, you know Zhongli? Well! That saves me a lot of explaining.

111100309.text: I'm Hu Tao, the current director of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, responsible for... well, trifling matters having to do with mortality.

111100310.text: A satisfying trade to be in, though, and Wangsheng Funeral Parlor is well-known around town. Whatever the request, I'd be glad to hear it.

111100311.text: I don't think we fall into the "client" category.

111100312.text: Yeah, if we were looking for Wangsheng Funeral Parlor's help, this is hardly the place we would come to.

111100313.text: Ah but you see, I wasn't referring to clients in the business sense. Everyone who enters this mortal realm will be a client of mine.

111100316.text: Wangsheng Funeral Parlor welcomes advance reservations! When you choose us, you'll never have to worry about what might be around the corner.

111100317.text: But be sure to book the right date! Pro tip: it is a living nightmare trying to get flowers at short notice...

111100318.text: Speaking of dates, if you're struggling to decide, please do come and talk it over. I'd hate to see you still alive and kicking when your big day comes.

111100320.text: That's— You— ... There's a lot to unpack here...

111100323.text: You'll have to excuse her. The director is a rather unique individual. Allow me to explain.

111100324.text: We heard that there'd been some supernatural activity at Wuwang Hill. To restore calm here, we performed a funeral ceremony.

111100325.text: It went very smoothly! According to the director, we shouldn't be expecting any more issues in the near future.

111100326.text: Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, Wuwang Hill, funeral... What more is there to say? These three belong in the same sentence.

111100327.text: You two on the other hand, have no business coming to Wuwang Hill. You being here is not normal.

111100328.text: Umm... Maybe your understanding of "normal" isn't quite normal?

111100330.text: Adventure? Aha, you must hail from the Adventurers' Guild.

111100331.text: Then you are one of our distinguished clients! "Wood," to be precise.

111100333.text: That's just how we gauge our client's importance. We have four levels: "wicker," "bamboo," "wood," and "marble." The higher the grade, the better we'd like to get to know you.

111100334.text: But I've just only heard of this!

111100335.text: Well, that's because I only just thought of it. Oh, don't look so shocked.

111100336.text: Take a look, our adventurers spend the whole day scaling mountains, clearing domains, and smiting enemies. Danger and peril are their bread and butter.

111100337.text: Clients like these deserve better treatment. Taking an interest in their daily lives will ultimately benefit not only them, but also me...

subQuests.subQuestName: Accompany Hu Tao to the Adventurers' Guild

111100401.text: Ugh, you again... Look, I told you, we're not interested in the kind of cooperation you describe.

111100402.text: Come on, there's no reason to get upset. Look, one of your members is an avid supporter of my proposition!

111100405.text: Since our last negotiation, I've come up with a new proposal, which I think you'll find has far more benefits for you.

111100406.text: First things first, Wangsheng Funeral Parlor will prioritize the Adventurers' Guild requests above all others. You'll also receive 100 of our signature wooden coffins for free, together with your first order.

111100407.text: That's not all! We also provide an on-site cadaver collection service covering almost all regions in Liyue. Now, we do charge a slight premium for a very small number of especially dangerous areas, but... but don't you worry about that, I promise you it's still very affordable!

111100408.text: I don't think you're hearing me...

111100409.text: Okay, alright. I get it, you want to bargain a little more. But our offer as it stands is already quite a good deal, don't you think?

111100410.text: Just think about it. An adventurer's life is full of unexpected threats. It's only natural to take precautions. "Mend the roof before it rains," as they say.

111100411.text: Yeah... no. I'm not so sure that saying applies in this context.

111100412.text: Speaking of precautions, I'd rather focus on keeping my adventurers safe in the first place.

111100413.text: It's time for you to go. I have to attend to other matters.

111100414.text: Wait, hold on! Wh—What would you say to a group discount!? Thirty percent off for parties of ten!

111100415.text: Director! Please, you did your best... We don't need another clash with the Millelith.

111100416.text: Uh... If Paimon understood all that correctly, it seems like she's trying to sell them the funeral parlor's services.

subQuests.subQuestName: Go back to the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor with Hu Tao

111100501.text: *sigh* Seems like the old ways are the most reliable after all.

111100502.text: Meng, are you done preparing our promotional materials?

111100503.text: Ah... My apologies, I'm only about halfway through. Do you really think they'll be effective?

111100504.text: Trust me, they're going to work wonders. This marketing strategy has been used by Wangsheng Funeral Parlor for generations.

111100505.text: Clients in need come to our door and write down their commissions on blank wooden tiles. Then, they squeeze those inside the parlor through the crack under the door.

111100506.text: I fulfill the request written on each tile to make sure our clients are satisfied with the service, no matter if it's an obituary, cremation, or funeral that they seek.

111100507.text: Although... it is a bit of a hassle with the constant back and forth. If only we could burn 'em by the batch...

111100508.text: No, director, I'm not asking about the wooden tiles themselves but about the "special offer" they advertise.

111100511.text: Hehe, Wangsheng Funeral Parlor should keep up with the times! Just think about it! If we don't attract new clients, we'll be left with nothing, won't we?

111100512.text: Business development is a crucial element of every prosperous enterprise. I've been trying various marketing strategies ever since I became the director.

111100513.text: I put up posters, just like all the other shops, but the Millelith promptly removed them.

111100514.text: Then, I organized the "Wangsheng Visitor's Day," but no one showed up.

111100515.text: Well that doesn't come as a huge surprise...

111100516.text: And finally, I discovered that the traditional ways are the most reliable after all. I took inspiration from the wisdom of previous directors.

111100517.text: So now, I go from door to door, looking for people and organizations willing to cooperate. Just like during our visit to the Adventurers' Guild! That's what I mean by "business development."

111100518.text: The other method I'm trying is using the wooden tiles as coupons. Just by writing things like "Buy one, get one free for the holder of this tile" on them.

111100519.text: Wh—What do they buy and what do they get?

111100520.text: Hehe, a solid and durable "second home," of course.

111100521.text: They may not need it right away, but they can be sure that when they do, it will still be as good as new. "It won't start deteriorating before you finish doing so yourself" — that's the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor quality guarantee.

subQuests.subQuestName: Investigate the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor's surroundings while waiting for Hu Tao

111101301.text: (A board used for hanging Wangsheng Funeral Parlor's wooden tiles. According to Hu Tao, all the tiles should be blank...)

111101302.text: (...In which case, the characters on the back of the tiles must be the "special offer.")

subQuests.subQuestName: Investigate the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor's surroundings while waiting for Hu Tao

111101401.text: (So, behind this door is Wangsheng Funeral Parlor...)

111101402.text: (It looks far more ordinary than the director made it out to be.)

subQuests.subQuestName: Investigate the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor's surroundings while waiting for Hu Tao

111101501.text: You must be the Director's new hires?

111101502.text: Not us! We're just very curious about Wangsheng Funeral Parlor and Hu Tao.

111101503.text: Well, I wouldn't get too curious if I were you. Too much knowledge isn't good for ordinary folk.

111101504.text: The director is tactful when it comes to what should and shouldn't be known.

111100701.text: That's settled then, write it like this:

111100702.text: "Wangsheng Funeral Parlor Bumper Sale! Buy One, Get One Free! Buy Two, Get Three Free! More For Your Mora!"

111100703.text: Hee-hee! I love it, better than all that lifeless brochure stuff. We want people to feel warm and fuzzy.

111100704.text: But Director... Isn't lifeless the name of the game in this industry?

111100705.text: That's old hat, we're opening up new ground.

111100706.text: Why does Wangsheng Funeral Parlor need to open up... *sigh* Yes, Director.

111100708.text: Right, we should get going. I am not letting new business escape us.

111100710.text: Who else? Do you see anyone else around here? ...Well, you probably wouldn't see them if there was.

111100711.text: Stop adding little afterthoughts like that! Creeps people out!

111100712.text: Hee-hee, just a joke, sorry. Everything you see is everything that's present. For the moment, at least.

111100715.text: Ah, lighten up! The way I see it, people make death scarier than it really is.

111100716.text: What people truly fear about departing this world is suffering and regret. To deal with the trauma, they let their imaginations run wild with notions of ghosts and evil spirits.

111100717.text: All baseless fantasies. What we've ended up with is a topic that people are morbidly afraid of talking about... If I don't broach the subject, then Wangsheng Funeral Parlor won't be long for this world.

111100719.text: Oh? More approachable and appeasable than you'd imagined?

111100720.text: Uhh, Paimon wouldn't say that. Let's just say, at least it didn't hurt us...

111100721.text: You must have come across a particularly ferocious entity. How should I put this... Most spirits are incapable of harming ordinary folks.

111100722.text: The job of Wangsheng Funeral Parlor is to "guard the border between life and death." One component of this is correcting notions of death and the afterlife that people may hold. Simply put, for those unable to see the "border," they're best kept as far away from it as possible.

111100723.text: So for ordinary folks, the best-case scenario is ignorance of all matters concerning spirits and the afterlife — or even better, a belief that none of it exists.

111100724.text: Then you really don't have any excuse for spooking the heck out of people!

111100725.text: Haha, you make it sound so abominable. I'm just trying to get them to see the humor in it all.

subQuests.subQuestName: Visit a potential client with Hu Tao

111100802.text: Hello! I'm Hu Tao, Director of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor.

111100803.text: Okay, so why would someone from Wangsheng Funeral Parlor be looking for me?

111100804.text: Mmm... nothing major. How are you feeling these days? Any aches or pains?

111100805.text: You shouldn't ignore them, by the way. Very often, they're an omen of something terminal.

111100806.text: When we're healthy, it's easy to forget the crushing fragility of life. So... aches and pains. Best to keep an eye on them.

111100807.text: What are you getting at!? I'm in great health and enjoying life very much, thank you!

111100808.text: Go and find some other poor soul! Goodbye!

111100901.text: Uh, and you are? Be quick, I'm busy.

111100902.text: Hello there, would you be interested in understanding a bit about our services at the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor?

111100903.text: Wangsheng Funeral Parlor? Uhhhh... I'm not in need of your services.

111100904.text: So you're out here... looking for new customers? Don't you think this might be a bit of a crass way of going about it?

111100905.text: Hardly. Isn't this the fashion these days? "Bring the service to the customer," and all that?

111100906.text: I'm not sure it's every service that falls into that...

111100907.text: Anyway, please bother someone else if you don't mind.

111101001.text: I know your face... The Wangsheng Funeral Parlor Director, right? Sorry, I'm really in no need of—

111101002.text: Don't apologize, get to know us! We've got a new sale going on.

111101003.text: Ever hear the saying "out with the old, in with the new"? Well, going out with a bang is the best way to start off in style on the other side! Hee-hee.

111101004.text: If you keep talking like this, I'll have to call the Millelith.

111101005.text: No no no — okay, relax, we're leaving.

111101006.text: But Wangsheng Funeral Parlor awaits your distinguished patronage.

111101007.text: You really don't give up, do you?

111101010.text: Hmm? Are you trying to make me feel better?

111101011.text: ...Thank you. Seems you understand me far better than most people.

111101012.text: Not really, this is just getting really uncomfortable...

111101013.text: Enough "business development." Please, help me find someone.

111101014.text: "Business development"? Is that what you see this as?

111101015.text: Surely you don't think all that was "business development"!?

111101016.text: Then what was it exactly!? Traumatization for its own sake!?

111101017.text: No no no, the "business development" ended after the discussion with the Adventurers' Guild!

111101018.text: I was helping to find somebody for Meng. You remember Big G?

111101101.text: I have a reputation for being a weirdo amongst the ranks of the Adventurers' Guild...

111101102.text: But it's only because they haven't had an opportunity to talk to Hu Tao.

111101201.text: Hmm... The way we're wording this lacks... warmth and sincerity.

111101202.text: If we're content to settle for just seeing people off, how can we give them a sense of really having "gained" something?

111101203.text: But... that's a tough feeling to convey in this industry...

111101204.text: Precisely the problem! If we can't get that feeling across, then how will we get return clients?

111101701.text: Stick close to the director, she knows what she's doing.

111101901.text: Don't bother me again! I'm doing just fine!

111102001.text: Please, bother someone else if you don't mind.

111102201.text: *sigh* Big G... How did it all turn out like this...

111102202.text: Ah, don't mind me, just thinking out loud.

111109902.text: Let's go after him, he might do something stupid.

111109903.text: Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, "the ones who no longer speak"... Did she mean talking to the dead?

111109905.text: Hmph, rejecting a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. It's their loss.

111109906.text: Some things are inevitable. It's only a matter of time.

111109909.text: To visit an important potential client. I'll lead the way.

111109910.text: Ugh, why do they get angry? What's wrong with a few earnest health tips?

111109911.text: Paimon thinks it's because they're coming from the director of a funeral parlor...

111109912.text: Ugh... another failure. Still, not the end of the world.

111109913.text: Paimon's curious, does this approach ever work out for you?
